learning: Iteration 4 showed that widening the outer pair to ±0.05 lowered oval progress (0.87 to 0.80) without fixing bend exits, and that kd 0.35 with kp 2.0 did not reduce oval oscillation (0.339 to 0.333). Controller damping alone is therefore a weak lever. Next, check whether the 12 mm footprint changes s-bend and slalom max_error (both near 0.061 to 0.062 in iterations 3 and 4) and whether oval oscillation moves. If it does not, the next step is geometry (forward row or wheel_track), not more damping.
notes: Builder's 12 mm footprint test on the iteration 3 best design, with the controller held at iteration 3 values so the footprint is the only change.
rationale: Iteration 3 is the best raced design (203.20). Its oval max_error fell to 0.0598 and progress rose to 0.87, but oval oscillation was 0.339 and the s-bend and slalom still exit near 0.06. Iteration 4 widened the outer pair to ±0.05 and softened the controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.35). It scored lower (187.24), oval progress fell to 0.80, and oscillation stayed near 0.33, so the controller change did not reduce oscillation. The Builder's proposal keeps the iteration 3 geometry (±0.04 at y=0.06, body_length 0.22, wheel_track 0.09, mass 0.5) and changes only sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012. To keep this a single-variable test, I hold the controller at the iteration 3 values (kp 2.2, kd 0.30, ki 0, base_speed 1.2, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Expected result: a score near 203 if the footprint is neutral, or better s-bend/slalom max_error if smaller footprints react more sharply at the bend exit. If line_loss rises above 1.0 on any track, the 12 mm footprints are not helping.
